order.summary: Artifact metadata, blobs and deletion tombstones.
The audit and event journal through the snapshot watermark; events after it belong to the next backup.
Non-secret configuration and workspace registry revisions.
Context and compression manifests, memory and search state, skills, learning and curator state, profiles, goals, automations, boards and trigger definitions.
The exact corresponding source and dependency locks for the last known-good seed.
The database plus snapshot metadata consistent with its write-ahead log, taken through the supported online backup mechanism.
An independently checksummed disconnected-start bundle.
The last known-good seed and bootstrap verifier for development-plane recovery, backed up separately from production.
Policy, persona, command and companion bundle hashes.
Encrypted credential ciphertext with a separately escrowed rotatable key, or external secret-provider references with independently recoverable version metadata. Never a plaintext export.
Current and previous release manifests, schemas and SDK compatibility metadata.
Tool, MCP, extension and hook manifests with their enabled and quarantine revisions.
The drill verifies artifact hashes against the restored artifact metadata.
The drill verifies database integrity before anything downstream is trusted.
Development-plane recovery checks the disconnected-start bundle against its independent checksum and its corresponding source.
The drill verifies release and configuration manifests against the restored revisions.
The drill verifies policy versions against the restored bundle hashes.
Startup in disconnected recovery mode, with no external transport and no provider start, before any transport lease can be acquired.
Each required credential descriptor resolves to its expected secret version through the selected recovery path, without exposing a value. Metadata alone is not a recoverable backup.
The audiences and tenants of the resolved credentials are revalidated before anything external is enabled.
Transport intake, outbox delivery, provider starts and connector sends stay disabled until the credentials resolve and their audiences and tenants are revalidated.

excluded.summary: Private release-signing, protected-branch and deployment credentials are never part of candidate or ordinary lab recovery, so a drill that needs them is testing the wrong boundary.
